learner_operation: Find the number of pivot columns of a general matrix by elementary row reduction to REF and counting its nonzero rows/pivots.

fixed_features.feature: Count pivot columns, with five numeric radio choices.
fixed_features.justification: All 17 assessed source questions use this task and response contract; the canonical example also asks the count.

fixed_features.feature: Sparse numeric matrices, short elementary row replacement reduction to REF.
fixed_features.justification: Tutorial d45a4eba requires REF before identifying pivots; captured assessed sources use one or two row replacements. This preserves moderate workload.

fixed_features.feature: Source shapes and full bank profiles.
fixed_features.justification: These bound the observed workload and response domain; fixing the count within them is not justified.

answer_roles.role: Residual rows that vanish or survive after elimination
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Change zero residual to a later nonzero pivot within fixed shape and workload.
answer_roles.observed: Controlled rank 2→3 pair; delivered same 3x5 active-three group has ranks 3,3,2, and 4x5 active-four group ranks 4,3.

answer_roles.role: Pivot locations and dependent row assignment
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Vary ordered pivot columns, prefix sources and active rows while preserving a short valid elimination.
answer_roles.observed: Fresh normal samples cover every retained template; current branch uses explicit compatible rank/active assignments without changing elimination validity.

answer_roles.role: Matrix labels and correct choice positions
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Rename matrices and shuffle the full bank independently.
answer_roles.observed: Name counterfactual preserves matrix/rank; label, first-choice and bank-extreme probes have counterexamples. Small finite subgroup coincidences are documented.

coverage.result: 5/5 survive; ranks 2,3,4; both selected shape/active-row groups contain contrasting outcomes.

coverage.case: All 17 source workload/bank profiles and fresh normal samples
coverage.result: 17 complete source replays and 51 fresh normal samples pass independent exact checks. Author checker rerun supplies two contrasting ranks for every source workload; fresh independent batch seeds and counts also pass.

coverage.case: Retained defect is real and current revision changes its result
coverage.result: Strict original shortcut test exits 1 on old 5/5 failing pool and 0 on current batch. Relocated author assertion also fails on the old pool, then passes against current code.

counterfactuals.change: At fixed q-130957 parameters and seed 74109, change final residual row entry (3,5) from 0 to 1; exactly one input matrix cell changes.
counterfactuals.expected: Rank, selected numeric key and solution conclusion change from 2 to 3; prompt retains all other matrix entries. Native grader swaps acceptance of choices 2 and 3.
counterfactuals.observed: Independent exact ranks 2 and 3; prompt/solution stages agree; both rendered prompts show the one-cell difference. Native grader accepts 2 only before and 3 only after, rejecting the opposite choice.
counterfactuals.justification: The necessary operation is deciding whether elimination leaves a nonzero row; source f1ae8763 and 8a6c1395 demonstrate both outcomes.

counterfactuals.change: Rename matrix A to D with all matrix data fixed; separately rescale a nonzero echelon prefix row before reversing the fixed operations.
counterfactuals.expected: Rank remains 3; names update throughout prompt and explanation; keys still select 3, native grading preserves numerical choice acceptance.
counterfactuals.observed: Matrices identical under rename, names updated in rendered prompt/solution; rank unchanged under both irrelevant changes. Native grader accepts 3 and rejects all four alternatives for each.
counterfactuals.justification: Matrix names and invertible row rescaling do not alter pivot count; labels are incidental in all captured questions.

delivery.result: At captured basis 5362, batch survives 5/5 and normal controls 51/51 with identical ranks and choice semantics. No preparation file exists; shared tool runs actual prepare_records. Weighted moderate selection retains eligible contrasts; explicit history-subset scenarios are recorded, not asserted to be live histories.

limitations: No finite review proves absence of every incidental shortcut.
Source canonical example has no captured answer-control evidence; all 17 assessed source cases replayed, canonical mathematics confirmed.
Live selection policy, actual learner histories and future inventory/entity IDs are not captured. Hypothetical scenarios use explicitly synthetic IDs. Exhausted subsets can lose contrasts.
A three-sample q-73628 coincidence was challenged using independent prior seeds rerun on current code; ranks 2,3,4 remain available.
Captured inventory lacks generated metadata; no affected stored defect demonstrated and no generated identity invented.
